findings.title: Unconditional property access on `mainHostDestinationCalendar` throws `TypeError` when `destinationCalendar` is empty or null
findings.body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` is followed immediately by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining. Whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]` (which happens for any user without a configured destination calendar) and `evt.location === MeetLocationType`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and this line throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`, crashing booking creation.

findings.title: Co-hosts' destination calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set. On line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op because of optional chaining on `null`. In a collective event where the main host has no destination calendar configured (e.g., relying on fallback or no calendar) but other hosts do have destination calendars, all co-hosts' destination calendars are silently discarded and their calendar events are never created. Initialize `destinationCalendar` as `[]` or assign `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

findings.title: `calendar.events.patch` uses `undefined` `calendarId` instead of `"primary"` fallback
findings.body: Previously `selectedCalendar` defaulted to `"primary"`. After this change, `selectedCalendar` is `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, which is `undefined` when no matching entry exists (or `externalId` is not set). While `calendar.events.insert` uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` call (used to add the Google Meet `hangoutLink` to the event description) passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly, causing the patch request to fail with a missing `calendarId`.

findings.title: Fallback lookup in `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` searches for falsy `externalCalendarId`
findings.body: In `updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch of `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`""`, `null`, or `undefined`). Searching `event.destinationCalendar` for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` in that branch can therefore never match a valid calendar ID and will always evaluate to `undefined` (causing `updateEvent` to pass `calendarId: undefined` to Google Calendar API).

findings.title: Unrelated change inverts `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` condition for organization `slug`
findings.body: Line 151 changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. When team billing is enabled, organizations are supposed to store only `requestedSlug` in metadata until payment/verification completes, and only set `slug` directly when billing is disabled (`!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED`). Inverting this condition breaks organization creation when billing is disabled (slug is never set) and prematurely assigns the live slug before billing when billing is enabled. This also appears to be an accidental change unrelated to `destinationCalendar`.
